convention.domain: For q a nonnegative integer, b is a function from the named wires 0,...,q-1 to bits 0,1.
convention.wire_order: Wire zero is least significant. Strings and tuples in the lesson list wire zero first.
convention.closed_form: The recursion yields E_q(b)=sum over i<q of 2^i*b_i. Only its six-wire instance is explicitly claimed as a named fixed-width formula in this source.

independent_proofs.general_bijection: Induct on q. The empty wire set has exactly one function and Fin(1) has exactly zero. For j<2^(q+1), r=j mod 2 is a bit and k=floor(j/2)<2^q. Set the head to r and the tail to the induction inverse of k. Then r+2*k=j. Conversely b_0 in {0,1} ensures (b_0+2*k) mod 2=b_0 and floor((b_0+2*k)/2)=k, so the extracted tail and head recover b. The coordinate ordering of the product must be (tail,head) to obtain 2*tail+head.
independent_proofs.six_wire: Substitute the successor recursion six times; the q=0 residue is zero. The weights are 1,2,4,8,16,32 and the largest coordinate is their sum,63.
independent_proofs.two_wire_inverse: For 0<=j<4, quotient floor(j/2) is already a bit. The two returned bits are j mod 2 and floor(j/2) mod 2. Their E_2 sum is j. For each of four j, evaluate explicitly; the resulting table determines equality of the whole function and each projection.
independent_proofs.three_wire_inverse: For 0<=j<8, successive divisions by 2 recover bits at weights 1,2,4; floor(j/4)<2. The weighted sum of the three residues reconstructs j. Evaluate the eight j to establish both function and coordinate claims.
independent_proofs.restriction_semantics: A split at legal target t returns b(t) and b restricted to named wires unequal to t. Equality of the restricted functions is pointwise equality at all i != t; equality at t is irrelevant.
independent_proofs.two_wire_context: For t=0 the unique retained bit is wire 1=floor(j/2); for t=1 it is wire 0=j mod 2. Equality of a singleton-domain bit function is therefore equivalent to equality of the displayed code.
independent_proofs.three_wire_context: For t=0 the retained pair (wire1,wire2) has E_2 code floor(j/2). For t=1 the pair (wire0,wire2) has code j mod 2+2*floor(j/4). For t=2 the pair (wire0,wire1) has code j mod 4. Each code is injective on its pair: quotient and remainder by 2 recover both retained bits. Therefore context equality iff code equality in all three target cases.
independent_proofs.carrier_reexpression: 2^2=4 and 2^3=8. Writing Fin(2^q) instead of the corresponding numeral changes the presentation of the same bounded coordinate carrier, not the ordering or encoding. Substitution of the preceding inverse identities transports each context assertion to the grid presentation.

context_codes.code_ranges: Two-wire deletion codes are in {0,1}; three-wire deletion codes are in {0,1,2,3}.
context_codes.retained_order: Increasing original wire order, then compact little-endian weighting.
context_codes.middle_target_boundary: After deleting wire 1 in a three-wire state, original wire 2 receives weight 2, not 4.
context_codes.not_target_equality: For example indices 0 and 1 have equal contexts when deleting wire zero, despite differing target bits.
